reigns_index.h: 30 May 2003 · PCW (Primetime, 2000–2004)Gaz 'The Jester' Green — Continental Championship won at Fusion 124 until between 2003-06-25 and 2004-02-23 (circa) FUSION 124’S OWN SURVIVING PAGE DOES NOT CARRY THE MATCH IT ANNOUNCES. The page runs five matches and no Continental title match, while its own commentary books one for later the same night and the fed’s own next show replays that match’s finish as a main event. This is a page missing its own main event, not a week PCW staged nothing in: PCW’s own booking record carries seven shows between 25 May and 13 Jun 2003 and a results page survives for every one of them. Corroborated forward: PCW's own results page for Fusion 125, 6 Jun 2003 bills him "PCW’s Continental Champion" with "the PCW Continental title, resting shallowly upon his Persian sofa", and PCW's own results page for Turmoil 129, 12 Jun 2003 has him carry "his Continental Championship strap against his shoulder" throughout. The log stores Gaz Green on both sides of this row and is right; no correction is owed. Turmoil 130, 19 Jun 2003 — a disqualification win does not move a belt. PCW's own results page for Turmoil 130, 19 Jun 2003 bills "THE CURRENT CONTINENTAL CHAMPION, GAZ “THE JESTER” GREEN!!!!" and ends "WINNER BY DISQUALIFICATION: DANTE JACKSON"; six days later PCW's own results page for Turmoil 131, 25 Jun 2003 still bills "THE CURRENT PCW CONTINENTAL CHAMPION!!!! GAZ “THE JESTER” GREEN!!!!". The log itself records no change (champion before and after are both Gaz Green); the 2026 summary reads the DQ as a title change and the show record does not. Dante Jackson’s June 2003 – February 2004 "reign" is retired. No match ending this reign survives and no surviving page names a Continental champion between 25 Jun 2003 and 23 Feb 2004. PCW's own results page for Shanghaied IV, 23 Feb 2004 says in its own voice that the winner "will be crowned the first Continental Champion since the rebirth of PCW", so the belt lay unclaimed across the gap; how the reign ended the record does not say.

reigns_index.h: 3 July 2003 · eVolution (eVo)The Syndicate — Tag Team Championship won at eVo1: One Year Anniversary Show until 17 September 2003 The Syndicate won the Tag Team Championship when Big Daddy Dreamer powerslammed Eric Knight off a ladder through the ring and The HeartBreak Chick speared Deacon, and the referee counted three. Defences on record. Legends XLII, 9 July 2003: The Syndicate kept the Tag Team Championship when The HeartBreak Chick pinned Blackman1, in a match the header billed Non-Title. Legends XLIII, 16 July 2003: The Syndicate kept the Tag Team Championship in an Iron Man match against The BodySnatchers by having won more falls when the time limit expired. ReVelations 2003, 27 July 2003: The Syndicate retained the Tag Team Championship in a War Games match when Big Daddy Dreamer made Dolo Bentswinger tap out to a dragon sleeper. X-Rated 2003, 31 August 2003: The Syndicate retained the Tag Team Championship when Luther Wisdom, billed Xerxes Democritus, turned on his partner Jason Relms and lay down for Big Daddy Dreamer's pin. Legends XLIX, 10 September 2003: The HeartBreak Chick rolled up Scott Frost in a small package, holding his tights, after a masked Strictly Prohibited (Jason Jameson) chaired Frost, to keep the Tag Team Championship for The Syndicate.

reigns_index.h: 2003-07 (month) · PTC (2002)Seymour Almasy (UWF) — PTC Global Championship until 2004-03 (month) (Won a 64-man PTC Invitational Tournament (PIT) for the vacant title. Successfully defended against Angelus Sorrow (31 Oct 2003) and against Dave Harley (WWA) in a Best 2-out-of-3 Falls match on RPW's Adrenaline programme (8 Feb 2004) — after which Chris Storm attacked Almasy with the title belt. Lost the title to Chris Storm and AWS Man (aka Bill) in March 2004.) TIER-3 MINT: this is Almasy's first of three PTC Global Championship reigns on the surviving record. "Following the match [the Chris Storm loss] the head of the PTC Global Title division stepped down and was replaced," per the same article. PTCpedia's own PTC Global Title article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-global-title.html, captured 19 Aug 2010) — a fuller, later-compiled title history than the alliance news engine's own partial lineage; per docs/PROCESS.md's hub rule, its claims corroborate the existing record rather than override it. A second federation's own document places the belt on him inside this reign: Lights Out Wrestling's own page for Wakeup Call, 31 August 2003 (/promotions/low/archive/wakeup-call-2003-08-31.html), bills him “not only the World Champion of the Universal Wrestling Federation, but the Global Champion for the entire Primetime Central Television Network”, and says his Xtreme Title challenge that night was first booked title-versus-title, with “Almasy adding the PTC Global Championship to the mix”. PTCpedia's own 2008 revision of his article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-seymour-almasy-2008.html) tells the same reign again and adds that he “would hold the title for almost nine months” and “would be the only champion to successfully defend his title until XUW's Saij”.

reigns_index.h: 31 August 2003 · eVolution (eVo)Thug roC — United Championship won at X-Rated 2003 until 10 December 2003 Thug roC pinned Ryan Mason with the roCing Horse after a chair shot to win the Continental and ULWN titles together and become the first United Champion. Defences on record. Legends XLIX, 10 September 2003: Thug roC pinned Yoshii Tanaka with the roCing Horse to retain the United Championship in its first defence. Legends L, 17 September 2003: Thug roC retained the United Championship when Aaron Justice ran in and pushed Scott Evans's shoulders down during a small package, and the referee counted three. Legends LI, 24 September 2003: Thug roC pinned Tok'n with the roCing Horse after the Lethal Injection to retain the United Championship, in a match the header billed Non-Title. Digital Destruction 2003, 5 October 2003: Thug roC saved the United Championship in the second fall by clotheslining QBX and hitting him with the tag belt before the referee saw Shaft-Man tap, then pinning him. Legends LIII, 15 October 2003: Scott Evans's interference gave Shane Wethers the win by disqualification over Thug roC, who kept the United Championship. Faith 2003, 9 November 2003: Thug roC pushed the ladder over, hit Scott Evans with the roCing Horse onto it and unhooked the belt to retain the United Championship in a ladder match. Legends LVII, 26 November 2003: Thug roC pinned Matt Hunt with the roCing Horse to retain the United Championship in a four corners match.

His third VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship reign; the loss returned Randall Crane to an in-storyline suspension both men had been serving since Vegas Violence III's own post-match assault. The Maquilladora's own scheduled challenge on the Kickoff Card (9 January 2004) was called off by order of new co-owner Classy Joey Boy, who ruled he had already beaten The Maquilladora and would not face him again; Demonic and The Maquilladora wrestled a 24 Hour Contender Match instead, which The Maquilladora won. An unseen figure attacked the champion near a creek before Ghost Town Blues's own Pentagon match, keeping him from a scheduled title defense against the match's own winner; a stand-in triple threat settled that night's own live crowd stakes without changing the title. reigns_index.h: 17 December 2003 · UWF (23 Mar 1996)Papa Legba — UWF Meltdown Championship won at UWF Meltdown, 17 December 2003 end unknown Won the inaugural UWF Meltdown Championship, surviving a fifteen-man battle royal as one of its own final four, beating Victor Frost in the semi-finals with an inverted DDT, then Paul Wong in the finals with the Black Magic superbomb. Retained against Alex Kidd on 10 March 2004 by pinfall (Ragga Bomb) with an assist from Tigress and Randall Osbourne. Attacked Alex Extreme and Randall Osbourne with a chair before the bell of a scheduled three-way defense on 21 March 2004, then postponed the match to a cage bout the following week without it ever starting, citing his own father's recent death. Retained again in the rescheduled steel cage match on 5 May 2004: Osbourne never entered after Alex Kidd attacked him before the bell, and Legba climbed out of the cage to the arena floor ahead of the remaining challenger, Alex Extreme, to win by escape. Retained again on 19 May 2004, teaming with Tigress to beat Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault in an intergender tag after a top-rope splash caught both opponents for the pin.

reigns_index.h: 23 February 2004 · PCW (Primetime, 2000–2004)Inphino Blitz — World Championship won at Shanghaied IV until 23 February 2004 Shanghaied IV, 23 Feb 2004 — the belt's last recorded night, and three things happen to it. Cal Roberts VACATES it himself in an in-ring promo ("So as of right now I officially vacate my World Championship title!"); the fed's own executives overrule him on the same page ("Hey Buzz you can't just give up a title you moron, it takes lots of paper work. You're still the champion and your match with Blitz is for the title"); and Inphino Blitz then beats him for it — "And the winner... and NEW PCW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION... THE BLACK DRAGON MASTER... INPHINOOOOOO BLITZ!!!" Minutes later Dick James and Alan Zoober take it off him in the aisle: "you, Inphino Blitz, just MIGHT get into the records books as the SHORTEST REIGNING PCW WORLD CHAMPION EVER!! Cause of right now, YOU'RE STRIPPED!!!", adding "no matter the winner... the belt was getting vacated IMMEDIATELY AFTER" (PCW's own results page for Shanghaied IV, 23 Feb 2004). The fed uses both its words in one segment — STRIPPED for the act and vacated for the result — and the reign's end is filed under the word for the act. Blitz then lays the belt down himself rather than fight for it. His reign is the shortest of the belt's recorded reigns. The fed's own title log records the outcome of the match as undetermined (its own champion-after value left blank); corrected below.

reigns_index.h: 15 May 2004 · UWF (23 Mar 1996)Donna Tetreault — UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World won at UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 15 May 2004 until 2005-05-19 (circa) Won the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World from Stephanie Harper in a career-first title win; a pair of brass knuckles was found at ringside afterward, though no one openly claimed them. Teamed with cornerman Simon O'Neal on 19 May 2004 in a losing challenge for the UWF Meltdown Championship against Tigress and champion Papa Legba, whose top-rope splash caught them both; the Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World was not at stake in that match. Retained against Stephanie Harper again at Gold Rush 2004 (5 June 2004), using brass knuckles and then a foreign object hidden in her own bandana for the Caress of Steel; knocked out manager Simon O'Neal after he proposed marriage to her in the ring afterward. Retained again over Brianna Landis by pinfall (the Dominion Day windmill suplex) on 18 September 2004, aided by a distraction belt shot from Landis's own tag partner, Tara "Sunburst" Marshall. Retained again over "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa by disqualification on 16 October 2004, after Ishikawa was found with a taser at ringside despite having the champion beaten clean moments earlier. Retained again over Kari Stevens by submission (a crossface, with salt and lemon juice rubbed into a cut over Stevens's own eye) on 30 October 2004.

Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 30 as 4 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 11 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Karina Wolfenden took the World Heavyweight Championship from Invincible Gabe at The Kannon Effect, a pay-per-view whose card is not held; the write-up of the next show has Gabe say he lay down for her. Defences on record. Adrenaline 30, 11 July 2004: Magnum Wolf swatted Tessa Windsor off the top rope with a steel chair and the bell rang, so the match ended with no decision and Karina Wolfenden kept the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 32, 25 July 2004: Karina Wolfenden hit Brian Arson with a Pump Dropkick and caught him in a Small Package for the three after Christian Alexander Kannon had a replay show Magnum Wolf knocking her foot off the rope and the match continued, so she retained the World Heavyweight Championship.

reigns_index.h: 17 May 2004 · VWF (Vegas, 2001–2005)Kevin Blair — VWF 24 Hour Championship won at The Gauntlet 2004 until 12 October 2004 (Pinned Thunder Valenkov with a back body drop onto Valenkov's own cane, Lucy, during the Gauntlet battle royal.) Attacked Valenkov, Ric Beauty and Rob Beauty with Lucy after his own earlier tag match, then won the title from Valenkov in the closing battle royal the same night. Retained the title by count-out against Flash on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after leaving the ring with the belt rather than answering the referee's count, which eliminated him from the Dog Days tournament; a further challenge from Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) ended with both men walking away from the ring before a decision, the title again not changing hands. Majority owner Kingston Cash declares the championship no longer recognized by the promotion on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) and tries to confiscate the belt; Blair refuses and strikes Cash down, keeping the belt in his own possession with no successor named. Still clutching the same belt, Blair loses to a returning Classy Joey Boy by disqualification in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004) after attacking the referee rather than give it up. Eliminated early from a VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004) after fleeing to the back with the belt; Adam Jennings wins the battle royal and is announced champion by the ring announcer, but Kingston Cash refuses to recognize the change unless Jennings physically takes the belt from Blair. Blair fails to appear for a signed follow-up against Jennings on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), ruled a no contest; Cash instead sends his own new bodyguard G-Gangsta after Jennings, no bell rung. Blair again fails to appear for a defense against Fast Eddie Cutlass on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), another no contest, and runs in with Lucy to chair Jennings after Jennings beats Gangsta later the same show; Cash books Blair against Jennings in an I Quit match for the title at Vegas Violence. Loses the title to Adam Jennings in an I Quit match at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), knocked into the referee before physically knocking Jennings around while refusing to let go of the belt himself; finally says the words after a powerslam over the top rope with both men still gripping the title, then speared, sedated and stretchered out.

reigns_index.h: 5 June 2004 · UWF (23 Mar 1996)One-Winged Angel — UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World won at UWF Gold Rush 2004 end unknown Won the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Michael Bonn at Gold Rush 2004, a career-first title win in the held record; cornerwoman Ami Tran and Amity stablemate Spice each ran interference at ringside during the match. Retained again over Michael Bonn in a Gold Rush rematch on 28 August 2004, catching a top-rope hurricanrana attempt and turning it into the Revelator for the pin. Retained again over Chris O'Brien in a friendly MBC-reunion contest on 22 September 2004, finishing with the Heavenly Wind and Hell's Halo combination, dubbed "Divine Intervention" by cornerwoman Ami Tran. Retained again over Youth Gone Wild by pinfall (a top-rope german release suplex) on 25 May 2005, a tightly wrestled, mutually respectful contest. Retained again over Vyolynce by disqualification on 11 June 2005, after Vyolynce refused to break a rope-break leg hold. Lost the title to Jacob Drake in a bout not read by this collection, recapped on commentary during UWF Meltdown, 20 July 2005.

reigns_index.h: 5 June 2004 · UWF (23 Mar 1996)Kyle Lee — UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World won at UWF Gold Rush 2004 until 28 May 2005 Won the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World from Michael Augustine in the Gold Rush 2004 main event triple threat, also involving Edmond Winston IV, capping a year-long rise from a non-wrestling authority-figure role to the sport's top title; embraced manager Tesla St. James in the ring afterward. Retained over Jamie Underwood by disqualification on 18 September 2004 after owner Edmond Winston IV struck him with a steel chair, then superplexed him from the top rope through a steel ladder propped against the ring apron; Tesla St. James was knocked out trying to fight Winston off. Retained again over "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez by pinfall (a surprise inside cradle) on 11 December 2004, denying Martinez the title and Luke Kinsey his own promised shot at it for Rise to Power.

reigns_index.h: 10 July 2004 · LOW (2002)Psymon — LOW Xtreme Championship until 23 October 2004 (Beat Soma for the belt, in Psymon's own words in a served roleplay: "on July the tenth, I win the Extreme Championship against Soma in a Junkyard Match, cutting his title reign at a premature week".) Ends at the fed's own CATASTROPHIC pay-per-view of 23 October 2004, where Psymon defends the belt against Juvian Ramorez in a 2 out of 3 Falls Match and loses it (see r004): 105 days by the two dates. Psymon's own roleplay before that show calls him the longest-reigning Extreme Champion. Soma's own short reign before this one ("a premature week", in Psymon's words) is not dated by any surviving page. The fed's own champion banner has no capture inside this reign. An earlier reading credited this reign to Ramorez; the "July 10-current" line is on Psymon's card, and Ramorez's own card (captured 8 December 2004, served at promotions/low/archive/juvian-ramorez-bio-card.html) reads "Extreme Title(x1)".

reigns_index.h: 22 September 2004 · UWF (23 Mar 1996)Tigress — UWF Meltdown Championship won at UWF Meltdown until 22 June 2005 Won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Collision Holly in what was billed as a three-way submissions match; Vyolynce refused to participate and left the ring before the bell, leaving Tigress to beat Holly alone. Retained again over Youth Gone Wild by submission (an inverted dragon sleeper) on 6 October 2004. Retained again over Bobby Nash by pinfall (the Sumatran Headhunter, using the ropes for leverage) on 20 October 2004. Retained again over "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn by disqualification on 3 November 2004, after a UWF tryout group led by a disguised T.D. Swagger ran in. Retained again over Scorpio by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 17 November 2004. A defense against Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 1 December 2004 ended in a double disqualification draw after both wrestlers fouled each other simultaneously; the title did not change hands. A defense against Marissa Monet on 25 May 2005 also ended in a double disqualification, after both wrestlers shoved the referee; the title did not change hands. Retained again over Marissa Monet by submission (a modified Marjara Mallaka surfboard) in a No DQ rematch on 8 June 2005, the title's own last defense before its unification with the Rampage Championship the following week. Lost the title to Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit by pinfall (the 51st Drop) in a title unification match on 22 June 2005, ending the Meltdown Championship's own separate history.

reigns_index.h: 12 October 2004 · VWF (Vegas, 2001–2005)Adam "The Hype" Jennings — VWF 24 Hour Championship won at Vegas Violence IV end unknown (Forced champion Kevin Blair, who never released his own grip on the belt, to say the words in an I Quit match after a powerslam over the top rope left both men still holding the title.) Chairs a recovering Sebastian and G-Gangsta backstage the same night. Retains against a masked Billy Bones, billed The Masked Nevadan, on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), forcing the tap with the Hyper Driver before Robbie Caldwell unmasks and tazes the champion in a post-match attack chased off by Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov. Retains again over Robbie Caldwell in a Bring Your Own Weapons match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), finishing him with the Hyper Driver moments after ringside legend Johnny "Hands Of" Stone reclaims his own prosthetic leg, which Caldwell had used as a weapon on the champion. Retains against Paddy O'Shea at March To Madness (2 March 2005) by disqualification after Frank O'Shea's own interference. Retains against the debuting Mad Bomber at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), the Bomber disqualified for refusing to let a bomb-sniffing dog search his pockets. Retains again over the Mad Bomber at End Of March (30 March 2005), pinning him while he is stuck in a bulky training suit. Retained without a challenge at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005): on the line, alongside the Submission and Hardcore Championships, in an eight-man elimination match, but champion Adam Jennings is the final survivor for his own side and is never eliminated.

Retains against The Maquilladora and Classy Joey Boy in a triple threat on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), pinning Classy Joey Boy with the Face Plant after Sebastian's own interference and a guest-referee stint from majority owner Kingston Cash. Retains again at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), entering the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal first by his own request rather than last as tradition dictates, and surviving as the sole man left in the ring after Thunder Valenkov, sent into a top rope that Hot Property forgets to pull down, goes over instead.

reigns_index.h: 12 October 2004 · VWF (Vegas, 2001–2005)Alcoholics Anonymous (Marcus O'Malley, Mark McQueen) — VWF Tag Team Championship won at Vegas Violence IV until 8 November 2004 (Mark McQueen submitted Real Deal with the Devils Snare after O'Malley and McQueen isolated an injured shoulder.) Lawyer RAR argues on behalf of the Rodeo Boys that the champions were never legitimate, since Billy Bones and Kenny Kidd were released rather than beaten for the belts; majority owner Kingston Cash reinstates the Rodeo Boys on the spot, who beat down the new champions with cowbells immediately after. No formal title reversal is shown. Retains against the Rodeo Boys on March To Hell (21 October 2004) when Kenny Kidd is disqualified for branding Marcus O'Malley with an iron; retains again on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) when a substitute Outlaw Morris Bass stands in for the hospitalized O'Malley and submits Billy Bones with the Devils Snare.

The VWF Hardcore Championship, also on the line in the same match, goes unaddressed in the decision and stays with Gods Tears. Defended together with the VWF Hardcore Championship against Gods Tears and Lark Fenriz in a Scaffold Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005); wins the overall match by outlasting both other men on the scaffold, but the broadcast states neither title changes hands. Defended against Fast Eddie Cutlass at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), declared a no contest after Gods Tears, Roadkill Rick, Adam Jennings and The Dark Monster Tai Angela all converge on Gods Tears mid-match. Loses the title to Roadkill Rick's own Texas Speedbump in an eight-man elimination match at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005) after Gods Tears attacks him from behind before the bell.

Retains by disqualification against Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov at End Of March (30 March 2005) after the returning Hot Property (Stevie Knight and Austin Lee) run in and help finish McQueen. A legal challenge filed the same night argues the win itself does not count, since Team Brittania was never a named, signed participant in the St Patricks Day match; incoming VWF ownership is left to decide the championship's own status. On The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), Team Brittania defends the titles, billed with a question mark over their own legitimacy, against a returning Henry Fish (billed Scott Starring) and an unidentified stand-in wrestling as the absent Van Wild, winning by pinfall; the team's own hired ring announcer, not the broadcast's regular ring announcer, declares them champions afterward. The same night the previous champions, Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov, billed "the unlikely tag team champions," lose their own tag match to Hot Property when Valenkov turns on McQueen; the VWF's incoming ownership still has not ruled on the championship's own disputed status.

The card of WorldWide 13 (19 May 2005) shows the change, in a backstage hallway: "Trey Tremendous is the new GCW Hardcore Champion!" Sources disagree — the federation's own Hardcore Title History page gives him one reign from 5-19-05 to its next row (No. 30, Bryan Mayhem, 3-17-10), and its Reign cell's '42 days' would end it on 30 June 2005; the cards break it twice. At Warpath 2005 (29 May 2005) Johnny Lexicon pins him across town for the belt and he takes it back in the ring the same night; at Dangerous Games 2005 (circa 28 Jul 2005) Alex Morgan pins him during his United States title defence and he takes it back at ringside after the bell. The page carries none of the four changes; the cards' reigns are recorded, as the page's own 18-minute reign No. 25 is.

reigns_index.h: 2005-05-19 (circa) · UWF (23 Mar 1996)Marcus Nuit — UWF Rampage Championship won at UWF Saturday Night Rampage until 22 June 2005 Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing and commentary; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which Nuit won the title from Rick Marley at the Rise to Power pre-show. Retained the title over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath by pinfall (a headscissors takedown into a cradle) on 28 May 2005, his own first Rampage title defense, declaring himself the "Renegade of Rampage" beforehand. Retained again over the Mercenary by pinfall (a senton splash) on 11 June 2005, the title's own last defense before its unification with the Meltdown Championship the following week. Marcus Nuit beat Meltdown Champion Tigress by pinfall (the 51st Drop) in a title unification match on 22 June 2005; the Rampage Championship was retired into a new Unified Television Championship, with Nuit becoming its first champion.

reigns_index.h: 8 August 2005 · GCW (gcwonline.net)The Guild — Tag Team Championship until between 2005-08-09 and 2006-03-21 (circa) The page's own Won From cell reads 'Stephens/Summers'. Sources disagree — the federation's own Tag Team Title History page gives The Guild this reign from 8-8-05 to 3-21-06, and no held card has The Guild holding the titles: they debut on WorldWide 21 (18 Aug 2005, "The Guild makes their debut"), lose a number-one contenders' match to The Regulators on WorldWide 23 (1 Sep 2005), are booked against Stephens and Summers for the titles at FallOut 2005 and never appear there ("It seems the Guild has gone missing"). The cards have Stephens and Summers the champions from Annihilation (28 Aug 2005) to FallOut, The Bloodlines from FallOut, and the division ended on Devil's Night 2005 (30 Oct 2005) with The Bloodlines "the last champions of record"; the page's next reign (No. 16, 3-21-06) is won from 'Vacant'. Both readings are recorded. Either way the reign did not pass to another team in a match: on the page the belts were vacant before reign No. 16, and on the cards the division ended with The Bloodlines. No card of the night of this change is held; the date is the federation's own title history's.

The fed's own card and its forum place the Scavenger Hunt on Super Series I, 6 November 2005: the forum calls Hoyt Williams the new Extreme Champion "now that Super Series has been posted for some time" on 12 November 2005 and names Rollins the new Global Champion on 23 November. PTCpedia's own article on Rollins has him "capturing the PTC Global Title from the Uber Judge", the reverse of the title article's order and of the forum's own list of title holders of 4 June 2006 ("Uber Judge (Won from Rich Rollins)"). One of only two competitors (with Angelo Deville, per Rollins' own trivia section) noted for a tournament-winning streak through the GTT/PIT/CW era; GTT5 winner. PTCpedia's own PTC Global Title article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-ptc-global-title.html, captured 19 Aug 2010) — a fuller, later-compiled title history than the alliance news engine's own partial lineage; per docs/PROCESS.md's hub rule, its claims corroborate the existing record rather than override it.

reigns_index.h: 27 January 2006 · VXW (2001)Justin Harper — VXW Spin The Wheel Television Championship won at Winter War II end unknown (Pinfall over Kagedo, not champion Lark Fenriz, inside a triple threat, after Kevin Simmons's own interference knocked Kagedo out cold and Harper hit a Spinebuster on Fenriz before covering the fallen Kagedo for the three count.) Harper's own first title win in the held record. His own next match on record, against Roman Anderson on Winter War III, was explicitly billed non-title and is not treated as a defense. Retained the title in a scored Taipei Death Match against the same challenger, Roman Anderson, at St Patricks Day Massacre, a stipulation decreed by new 49 percent owner Lark Fenriz. Retained again in a twenty-minute time-limit draw against Omega at Hotter Than Hell I. Fought John Manning to a further time-limit draw at Sin City Fights August 31, in a match the broadcast's own commentary questioned the title status of after co-owner Spartacus's earlier title-stripping spree reportedly overlooked Harper; co-owner Ric Beauty publicly recognized Harper as champion on Sin City Fights September 19, setting a defense against Lance Voltar (winner of the TV Title Open Match's own Ring Two) at Vegas Violence. Retained again over 'The Big V' Lance Voltar at Vegas Violence 2006, opening the show with a Wipeout after kicking out of a top-rope corkscrew elbow.

reigns_index.h: 20 March 2006 · VXW (2001)Damian Payne — VXW Spin The Wheel Championship won at St Patricks Day Massacre end unknown (Pinfall, the Last Stop followed by a Chokebomb.) Payne's own second VXW Spin The Wheel Championship win, regaining the title he lost to Cobra twelve days earlier at Xtreme Machine I. Cobra repeatedly claimed the championship on air across the promotion's later broadcasts, defending it in matches billed as title defenses against Mr. Jones (The Hype II), Mr. Sal (The Hype IV) and John Manning (Hotter Than Hell I), but no surviving card ever bills or records a title change away from Payne. Payne remains this championship's last documented holder through the promotion's final surviving broadcast, Sin City Fights February 7, 2007, where he wrestles a non-title match unrelated to the championship.

reigns_index.h: 21 March 2006 · GCW (gcwonline.net)Seymour Almasy/Virgil Ambrosi (Seymour Almasy, Virgil Ambrosi, Eva VanLorne) — Tag Team Championship until 7 May 2006 Sources disagree — the record does not agree on who held this reign. (1) The federation's own Tag Team Title History page lists reign No. 16 verbatim as 'Seymour Almasy/Virgil Ambrosi | 3-21-06 | WorldWide | Vacant' — two names. (2) The same page's row for reign No. 17 reads 'UNITE | 5-7-06 | Meltdown | Eva/Ambrosi' — so the page names Eva and Ambrosi as the pair UNITE took the belts from. (3) Seymour Almasy's own bio card, in its Fed Titles line, verbatim: 'GCW World Tag Team Champion (w/ Eva VanLorne and Virgil Ambrosi)' — one championship, three names. (4) Eva VanLorne's own bio card claims the tag title herself: 'GCW Tag Team Title, GCW US Championx2, GCW TV Title Champ', and her two United States reigns and the Television title are all independently on the federation's own pages. Virgil Ambrosi's bio card carries no Fed Titles line at all, so it corroborates neither reading. Corroborating the partnership only, not the title: the fed's own card of WorldWide of 28 Oct 2005, a Tag Team Match, is billed 'Eva VanLorne & Seymour Almasy vs. Rich Rollins & Jonathan Borealis' — Eva VanLorne was his tag partner in GCW five months before this reign. All three are filed as holders here, and the page's two-name row and its reign-17 row are recorded above. The fed's own roster holds a page for each of the three and none for a team. No card of the night of this change is held; the date is the federation's own title history's.

reigns_index.h: 24 March 2006 · AWC (Atlantic Wrestling Club, 2005–2006)The Illustrious Face-Eater — Transatlantic Championship won at Twilight Of The Gods 2006 until 4 July 2006 Sources disagree — The fed's own title history ends Jack Murphy's reign on 24 March 2006 and lists no belt reign for Adam Dick after it (his line, the crown, runs from 17 January to 1 September 2006); the write-up has Dick win the belt from Murphy at Twilight Of The Gods. The fed's own title history has no vacancy (Adam Dick from 17 January to 1 September 2006, with Pierce Lavelle's third reign from 1 August concurrent); the write-up has Dick throw the belt down on 4 July 2006 and the belt left vacant. Adam Dick lifted Jack Murphy and dropped him on his head with Murphy's own Fall From Grace and pinned him to win the Transatlantic Championship; James Brunt refused to announce it. Defences on record. Fresh!, 9 May 2006: Adam Dick faked an injury after falling out of the ring, kicked out of Darcy Crisis's pin and hit the Eaterplex '05 to pin him and retain the Transatlantic Championship. Fresh!, 13 June 2006: Adam Dick hit Tim Martin with the Eaterplex '05 and pinned him while Ellis Nash kicked out of Liam Martin's cover, and James Brunt announced that Dick was still Transatlantic champion. Divide And Conquer 2006 (pay-per-view), 23 June 2006: Adam Dick hit Mike Wade with the Finger Poke Of Doom and covered him, and the two Unfuckables embraced after the count; Pearl then sent Michael Ryan home and ordered the match run again with Jack Murphy as referee. Divide And Conquer 2006 (pay-per-view), 23 June 2006: Mike Wade kicked out of Adam Dick's Eaterplex '05, then Dick reversed Wade's roll-up into a pin, with Jack Murphy as referee, to keep the Transatlantic Championship. Adam Dick threw the Transatlantic belt on the ground in front of Pearl and kept the crown as his own; the belt was left vacant and there was no match.

Fresh!east, 11 July 2006: Vince Jones stood over Leviathan, who was out cold beside a broken bat, and referee Aaron Davies counted the sudden-death fall, so Jones retained the Countdown Trophy. Fresh!special: Live On Huntington Beach, 1 August 2006: Garbage Bag Johnny burned Vince Jones out of the Ruby's Surf City Diner match with a flaming mop; Jones was still announced as the winner of the Countdown Trophy match and kept the trophy.

reigns_index.h: 1 September 2006 · AWC (Atlantic Wrestling Club, 2005–2006)Darcy Crisis — Frontier Championship won at Coast To Coast 2006 until 24 November 2006 Tony Little grabbed Anton Assault's leg, and Darcy Crisis hit the Mind Crisis and locked in his finishing hold, and Assault tapped before Billy Mays could break it up, so Crisis won the AWC Frontier Championship. Defences on record. Fresh!, 3 October 2006: Darcy Crisis held the Darcinator on Johnny Lexicon, who tapped while the referee looked away, and the referee called the bell only when Commissioner Wade came out, so Crisis retained the AWC Frontier Championship. Fresh!, 24 October 2006: Darcy Crisis locked in the Darcinator and AgentDash tapped while Michael Ryan looked the other way, so Crisis retained the AWC Frontier Championship when the bell finally rang. Fresh!special - Hallowe'en Edition, 31 October 2006: Darcy Crisis hit Tyson DeBough with a brainbuster and locked in the Darcinator, and DeBough tapped out, so Crisis retained the AWC Frontier Championship. Fresh!, 7 November 2006: Darcy Crisis turned an ankle lock into the Darcinator on Aimz, who tapped, so Crisis retained the AWC Frontier Championship. Fresh!, 14 November 2006: Darcy Crisis retained the AWC Frontier Championship by disqualification when the man in grey ran in and dropkicked Jack Murphy as Murphy was close to a fall.

reigns_index.h: 5 October 2006 · VXW (2001)Thunder Valenkov — VXW 24 Hour Championship won at Vegas Violence 2006 end unknown (Pinfall, a Thunder Bomb, for the title left vacant by Adam Jennings's own suspension, at the end of a mid-year tournament (a Second Chance Battle Royal and four quarterfinals narrowing to a Final Four, then a Vegas Violence final).) Valenkov's second documented VXW 24 Hour Championship win (this broadcast introduces him as 'the three time former 24 Hour Champion,' a claim the held record's documented history does not fully account for). Omega's own manager Richard Masterson secretly conspired with Valenkov's manager Chris Wheeling, saying something to Omega mid-match that left him open to the Thunder Bomb; Valenkov refused Wheeling's demand to attack the beaten Omega afterward. Manager Chris Wheeling wore the belt himself in a mock celebration and continued to lead Valenkov to the ring wearing it through Sin City Fights October 16 and October 24, without a title defense on either broadcast. Still without a defense, Wheeling gave Valenkov a night off from wearing the belt to the ring on Sin City Fights November 18 in order to wrestle a non-title match himself in Valenkov's place, then had Valenkov stand ringside without it again on Sin City Fights November 27. Contested again in a three-way match against Television Champion Cobra and challenger Miles McKinley at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, under special rules barring Valenkov from losing the title to McKinley; the match ended without a decision when the referee called for the bell amid a mass brawl, Valenkov still champion.

On Revolution in June Punk knocks out Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas with the belt, and at Wrestlepalooza Vito Thomaselli turns on him with a chair; the belt is not defended in this range, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, having been powerbombed through a table by Vito at Summer Assylum. reigns_index.h: 2007-02 (month) · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)Raven — ECW World Heavyweight Championship until 1 October 2007 (Raven's sixth reign in the diary's own history: he beats Sabu on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of February 2007 with an Evenflow DDT after Paul Burchill hits Sabu in the face with the Television Title and Goliath knocks him off the ropes, re-forms the Nest by throwing Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through ringside tables, keeps the belt against Shane Douglas at Baptism Of Fire on 29 March 2007 (with CM Punk's interference and three Evenflow DDTs, the last on a chair), which gives him Douglas's powers as commissioner, and is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam he keeps the belt over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match when Paul Burchill, the special referee, counts fast and calls a submission Rhino never gave, and Burchill then turns on him with a C-4; at Hardcore Heaven, in a match that is not for the title, he beats Burchill after CM Punk threatens to throw Kelly Thomaselli off the stage, and he is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end, with Owen Hart booked to challenge him at Wrestlepalooza and Bret Hart in a Triangle Match for the belt. At Wrestlepalooza Raven keeps the belt in the elimination Triangle Match when Bret and Owen Hart quarrel, Owen makes Bret tap to the Ankle Lock, and Raven hits Owen with the Raven Effect onto a chair; the giant in black, the mystery signing Mark Calaway, Chokeslams him, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman forces him into a non-title match with Vito Thomaselli, where Calaway's Chokeslam lets Vito pin him. At Summer Assylum he keeps the belt over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway and Raven covers, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Vito Thomaselli asking Paul Heyman for the title match at Heatwave. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Barbed Wire Cage Match Raven names, Vito Thomaselli beats him (Burchill's Corkscrew Cross Body from the top of the cage, then the Vito Driver) and is presented with the belt, but CM Punk hits Burchill with the International All Action belt and Vito with a GTS and carries the belt to Raven; on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven reads out clause 17.2a of the contract (interference from any party voids any title change) and says the belt still belongs to him and that Vito was never champion. Rhino wins the first Buck Stops Here Match at Heatwave to become number one contender and is booked against Raven at Anarchy Rulz; Raven is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Raven beats Rhino with Mark Calaway's help (Calaway's Elevated Powerbomb and Chokeslam, and Raven pins Rhino) and is then chokeslammed by Calaway. On Revolution on 1 October 2007 Owen Hart makes him tap to the Sharpshooter after Chris Jericho's chair shot: the reign ends there.) The diary's own history gives this reign's start as "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the win is filed at month precision (the text places it the night after Living Dangerously); the history's end of 1 October 2007 is the Revolution of October's first week (PDF p.1448), where Owen Hart makes Raven tap.

At Cyberslam they keep the belts over Los Increibles in the Ladder Match when Rob Van Dam pulls them down; at Hardcore Heaven Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone while Van Dam helps Traci, keeps them over the Canadian Connection with a third Sweet Chin Music on Christian; the champions quarrel through June but are still champions when the pages of June 2007's second week end. At Wrestlepalooza they keep the belts over the Hardcore Innovators when Michaels's Diving Elbow and Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash win simultaneous covers; the Dudley Boyz win the number one contendership on Blood, Sweat and Beers and, at Summer Assylum, the Whole F**kin' Show beat them in the Tables Match with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table on D-Von; they are still champions when the pages of August 2007's first week end. reigns_index.h: 10 May 2007 · GCW (gcwonline.net)Jay Terror — HDTV Championship won at WorldWide 67 until 14 October 2007 Sources disagree — the federation's own record carries a de-facto / de-jure split across the last two months of this reign, and both halves are recorded. Tyson DeBough physically took the belt at Tsunami of 12 Aug 2007 and kept it. The fed's own newsdesk of 5 Sep 2007: "Yes, Jay Terror is still the GCW Television Champion, and the records will continue to indicate as much. Tyson DeBough stole the title, and the only reason he still has it is because President Caldera seems to admire the moxie." Of 13 Aug 2007, DeBough's own claim — "Steal? I just took what was rightfully mine. I earned the right to wear this belt." — against the interviewer's — "But Terror never lost to you, or O'Shea. He is the rightful champion." The Television Title History page agrees with the newsdesk and dates the change to Dangerous Games: "After stealing Terror's Television Title belt and keeping it under the protection of President Caldera for almost a month, Tyson DeBough got a chance to win the title outright at Dangerous Games in a ladder match. Terror was stunned by DeBough who took the title home fairly." The reign is filed to 14 Oct 2007, the date the page and the newsdesk both give; the two months DeBough held the physical belt are recorded here and not as a reign of his own. The page's own Reign cell reads '157 days'. At Warpath 2007 (3 Jun 2007) he unified this belt with the Vanguard Championship, beating Katie O'Clare under Vanguard Rules.

reigns_index.h: 29 May 2007 · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)AJ Styles — ECW World Television Championship until 28 September 2007 (AJ Styles's first Television reign in the diary's own history: he debuts on Blood, Sweat and Beers in May 2007, turns on Rob Van Dam and Traci with the Canadian Connection and wins the belt at Hardcore Heaven; he beats Rey Mysterio Jr. with a low blow and a small package, takes a second defence on Revolution in June with an illegal use of the ropes, loses a non-title match to Juventud Guerrera, and is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June he beats Juventud Guerrera with a low blow and the Styles Clash, and at Wrestlepalooza he keeps the belt over Guerrera when Styles pushes Guerrera's foot off the rope before the Styles Clash is counted and Jim Molineaux does not see it; at Summer Assylum he keeps it again when Francine pretends to turn on Guerrera and Christopher Daniels, aligned with Styles, hits Guerrera with the belt; he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Guerrera's challenge for Heatwave on 28 August unanswered and Ultimo Dragon billed against him. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Stairway To Hell Match, Styles keeps the belt over Juventud Guerrera, who loses his mask: it hangs from one hook and the belt from the other; on Blood, Sweat and Beers in September he keeps it again, beating Jerry Lynn with a roll-up after pointing at the entrance-way to make Lynn look for Kurt Angle; he is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end, with Ultimo Dragon booked against him at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Ultimo Dragon pins him with an Asai DDT after Styles drags Francine into the ring and Dragon cuts off a Styles Clash with an elbow: the reign ends there.) The diary's own history dates the win 29 May 2007 and the loss 28 September 2007, Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1413), where Ultimo Dragon pins Styles with the Asai DDT.

reigns_index.h: 24 August 2007 · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)The Hardcore Innovators (Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer) (Cactus Jack, Tommy Dreamer) — ECW Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship until 26 October 2007 (Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer beat the Dudley Boyz for the belts at Heatwave: the Innovators cane the second generation of Dudleyz on the outside, Cactus Jack's Double Arm DDT catches Bubba Ray as he rebounds, Dreamer rakes D-Von's eye, and the two put D-Von through a table with a Double DDT before Cactus covers (1...2...3). Joey Styles says the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship has become the ECW Hardcore Championship, the diary's later previews call the belts the (newly rechristened) ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, and the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new champions after the match. In September, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, the Innovators ask the World Tag Team Champions for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz to crown the Undisputed Tag Team Champions; they are still the holders when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the Innovators lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest when the Dudley Family run in; in October, with Beulah McGillicutty, they ask Paul Heyman for a Singapore Cane Match, and at Guilty As Charged they are eliminated in the Three Way Dance (Bubba Ray pins Tommy Dreamer, then Cactus Jack): the reign ends there, 26 October 2007, though they leave the arena with all four belts and take them again from ringside after beating the second generation of Dudleyz on Blood, Sweat and Beers.) The belt is the Dudleyz's own, made and named by them on screen and won from them here. The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists it and dates this reign 24 August 2007 (Heatwave) to 26 October 2007 (Guilty As Charged). The diary's text calls the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship after this match; the title's own page keeps the name the Dudleyz gave it.

reigns_index.h: 14 October 2007 · GCW (gcwonline.net)Tyson DeBough — HDTV Championship won at Dangerous Games 2007 until 12 January 2008 Sources disagree — the federation's own record carries a de-facto / de-jure split across the two months before this reign, and both halves are recorded. Tyson DeBough physically took the belt at Tsunami of 12 Aug 2007 and kept it. The fed's own newsdesk of 5 Sep 2007: "Yes, Jay Terror is still the GCW Television Champion, and the records will continue to indicate as much. Tyson DeBough stole the title, and the only reason he still has it is because President Caldera seems to admire the moxie." Of 13 Aug 2007, DeBough's own claim — "Steal? I just took what was rightfully mine. I earned the right to wear this belt." — against the interviewer's — "But Terror never lost to you, or O'Shea. He is the rightful champion." The Television Title History page agrees with the newsdesk and dates the change to Dangerous Games: "After stealing Terror's Television Title belt and keeping it under the protection of President Caldera for almost a month, Tyson DeBough got a chance to win the title outright at Dangerous Games in a ladder match. Terror was stunned by DeBough who took the title home fairly." The reign is filed from 14 Oct 2007, the date the page and the newsdesk both give. The page's own Reign cell reads '90 days'; the page numbers this reign No. 28 and its own numbering repeats a number, so this reign is placed by the page's own order.

reigns_index.h: 26 October 2007 · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von) (Buh Buh Ray Dudley, D-Von Dudley) — ECW Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship until 30 November 2007 (The Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged, which the card bills as the match 'to unify the tag team championships', and take back the Dudleyville belts from the Hardcore Innovators; the Innovators leave with the belts, and retrieve all four again on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In November 2007 Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match at November To Remember XV in which the Dudley Boyz and the Hardcore Innovators unify the tag titles. At November To Remember XV the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; the Dudleyville belts are unified with the World Tag Team belts there, on the date (30 November 2007) the diary's history gives.) The history lists this belt separately and gives the reign as running to 30 November 2007, when it is 'unified with the World Tag Team Championship', and the text agrees: the unification is the Undisputed Tag Team Championship Match at November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707); the World Tag Team history treats the Dudley Boyz as holders of the undisputed titles from 26 October, and each history's date is filed in its own title.

reigns_index.h: 26 October 2007 · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)Raven — ECW World Heavyweight Championship until 30 November 2007 (Raven pins Jericho with the Commissioner's match and leaves with the belt as fans throw rubbish into the ring. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Don Callis apologises on the company's behalf and says that the win was legitimate under the promotional guidelines; the company's owner then returns, strips Raven of his powers as Commissioner, gives sole booking power to Paul Heyman and books Raven's defence at November To Remember XV against Paul Burchill: 'The natural order has been restored.' Raven is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as the champion and that Paul Burchill will beat him at November To Remember; Burchill, Vito Thomaselli and Chris Jericho beat members of Raven's Nest on Revolution and on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Heyman makes the title match a Loser Leaves ECW Match, with anyone outside it who touches either man to be fired and barred from signing with the Federation, and says that the man who stays will be the Undisputed ECW World Heavyweight Champion. Raven is still the champion when the diary's preview of the card ends. Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill at November To Remember XV (PDF p.1721) after a contest the diary rates A*: Burchill's C-4 from the top rope and a Shooting Star Press end the reign, and Raven, kneeling in the aisle, is out of ECW (the diary's next preview: 'Never again will Raven be seen in an ECW ring').) The history ends this reign on 30 November 2007, and the text agrees: the loss is the Loser Leaves ECW Match at November To Remember XV (Friday, week 4, November 2007, PDF p.1721); the history's date is the one filed.

reigns_index.h: 26 October 2007 · ECW Worldwide (Nevermore's diary)The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von) (Buh Buh Ray Dudley, D-Von Dudley) — ECW World Tag Team Championship until 4 November 2007 (The Dudley Boyz win the Ladders, Chairs, Canes and Flaming Tables Three Way Dance for both sets of tag belts: Bubba Ray eliminates D-Von's opponents in turn, and when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes Rob Van Dam out of the air he pins Van Dam. The Hardcore Innovators then leave the arena with the belts, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers the Innovators beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz and take all four belts from ringside again. In November 2007 the Hardcore Innovators still walk to the ring with all four belts, and Bubba Ray and D-Von challenge them for a title match at November To Remember XV; on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match in which the Dudley Boyz and the Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707) the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators, who carry both tag belts, in a weapons match with the Second Generation of Dudleyz and Daizy at ringside (a Superbomb through a table for Beulah McGillicutty, a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table for Tommy Dreamer, B) and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles. On Revolution on the first Monday of December they lose the Undisputed belts in a restarted Three Way Dance when Slyk Tayshaun Dudley makes Bubba Ray tap to the Boston Crabs.) The history ends this reign on 4 November 2007 and lists the Second Generation of Dudleyz (Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Slyk Tayshaun Dudley) as the champions from then, 'present'; the pages show something else: the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators at November To Remember XV (30 November), are called the first Undisputed ECW Tag Team Champions on the Saturday show and on Revolution, and lose the belts to Slyk and Dick Jr. on Revolution on the first Monday of December (PDF p.1747). The history's date is the one filed; the conflict is stated, not settled.

The history lists the reign as 'present', and the pages through the first Saturday of December show the champion keeping the belt (the diary's own preview of November To Remember XV and its Saturday show call him a new champion, a week after the win on 26 November); no end date is filed, and the record of these pages ends with Guerrera still the champion.

No reign changes there; his own reign begins at the Warpath ladder match.

reigns_index.h: 6 June 2008 · GCW (gcwonline.net)LeStatt Knight & Chris Storm — Tag Team Championship won at High Stakes 2008 until 2 July 2008 Sources disagree — the federation's own Tag Team Title History page dates this reign's win to 6-6-08 at High Stakes and names the holder 'LeStatt Knight & Chris Storm' jointly from that date. The fed's own news post ('Banned & Exiled~! Make History', 5 Feb 2009) gives a different mechanism: 'after LeStatt Knight had ended Banned & Exiled~! first record breaking title reign, he was forced into picking a partner by President Steven Caldera. At WorldWide 91, on June 18th, 2008, LeStatt Knight named Chris Storm his partner. Under GCW rules, this constituted as his second reign as World Tag Team champion since he had previously lost the belts.' On that reading Knight ended the Banned & Exiled~! reign alone around 6-6-08, and the joint Knight-and-Storm reign the page dates to that same day did not begin until Storm was named his partner twelve days later, at WorldWide 91 on 6-18-08. The article calls this the reign that makes Storm's later win over Oblivion (Feb 2009) his 'third reign... on account of a technicality', which is consistent with the count this reign already produces whichever exact date the joint reign began on. Filed on the page's own date; the news post's mechanism is recorded here rather than applied, and no separate WorldWide 91 reign is filed — the count the article itself gives is already satisfied without one. The page's own Won From cell reads 'Banned & Exiled~!'. The holder is the team 'Knight & Storm' that the fed's own title log names in the tag title match ('Knight & Storm vs. Samson & Delylah').

He keeps it through December 2008, beating Edd Stone with the Bloodstone Mutilation on Total Wrestling and Merle O'Curle in a non-title match on Badge of Honor; the diary's Psycho Circus preview treats the match that decides who faces him at Malice in Wonderland as a title unification match.)

The match that change is staged in sits on WorldWide of 2009-05-28 — the same day and month, one year later. Both readings are recorded; the reign follows the match's own show, because the page's own Reign cell for this reign ('112 days') is only reachable from a 2009-05-28 end, and the page's remaining tail rows then run in order (the cell reads '112 days' against the 113 the corrected dates give). His second reign, and his own bio card agrees: its Fed Titles line reads 'GCW Television Champion, GCW US Champion (x2)'. At the win Jacob McKail ran in with the American Dream and a referee and was thwarted when Taylor DDT'd the official; at the loss Tyson DeBough's cash-in landed. The fed's own title log spells the name both ways ('Zachariah Taylor' and 'Zacharia Taylor'); the page's own bio link for both reigns is Docta Z's.

reigns_index.h: 2 April 2009 · ACW (2002–13)Alias — ACW Scorpion Fighting Championship won at Courage, 2 April 2009 until 1 October 2009 Alias won the Scorpion Fight Night Challenge with 11 points, one more than Brian Spaes and Max Danger, to take the vacant Scorpion Fighting Title. Defences on record. Courage, 16 April 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by making Jimmy Cain submit to Anarchy's Lullaby. Courage, 30 April 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by making Rejection tap to Anarchy's Lullaby after a low blow. Courage, 7 May 2009: Alias kept the Scorpion Fighting Title when the match with Brian Spaes was ruled a no contest after a fan dived in front of Spaes's flying chair. Courage, 14 May 2009: Alias kept the Scorpion Fighting Title when the cage match with Brian Spaes was thrown out after Spaes speared him through the cage wall and tore it down. Legends III, 4 June 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by escaping the arena ahead of Brian Spaes in the empty-arena match. Courage, 25 June 2009: Alias kept the Scorpion Fighting Title when the match with Khristain Keller was ruled a no contest after Alias hit Keller with a chair. Courage, 9 July 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by pinning Frank Pierce with the A-Bomb. Courage, 23 July 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by making Iceman tap to Anarchy's Lullaby. Courage, 20 August 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by pinning Landon Stevens after throwing him into the arena door in a tailgate match. The Wake 2009, 17 September 2009: Alias retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by beating Khristain Keller three matches to two in the Five Stages of Grief series, which ended in a last man standing match.

Both readings are recorded. The reign is filed because the fed's own match text stages the change in full, and because the page's own numbers agree with it from both sides — its Reign cell on No. 31 reads '3 days' (2009-10-28 to 2009-10-31) and its No. 32 is dated to the 31st of October. It was Lantlas Anduril's own last match — 'it'll be the very last time he steps into the ring... ever' — and the fed staged Dan Black stealing the belt from him in the celebration. His own bio card fills Other Fed Titles only and claims no GCW title.

reigns_index.h: 31 October 2009 · GCW (gcwonline.net)Dan Black — United States Championship won at WorldWide 120 until 17 March 2010 Sources disagree — the page dates this reign '10-31-08' (2008-10-31) and links it to 'Digital Mortality vs. Zachariah Taylor' of 2008-10-09, a double-knockout no-decision in which Digital Mortality retains and Dan Black is not in the match; the change the text actually stages is at bout 2 of WorldWide 120 on 2009-10-31 — the same day and month, one year later. Both readings are recorded. The reign follows the match: the 2008 card's text excludes him, the card of 2009-12-16 has him defending as champion and names the American Dream as how he won it, and the 2008 reading would put this reign inside two other men's. The page's own Reign cell reads '--' and its own last cell reads '--', so the page claims no end for it. Defended on 2009-12-16 (beat AXEL Action) and at NC-17 on 2010-03-05, per the fed's own title log. His own bio card claims only 'GCW TV Champion' and no United States reign — recorded; the page, the title log and three match texts all carry the reign, and the card is simply short.

Courage 109, 1 April 2010: Alias kept the World Heavyweight Championship when his match with Keith Scott Zimmerman dissolved into a brawl after Shawn Jessica Hart rang the bell across the referee's face, and Trey Vincent's three count on Alias with no referee counted for nothing. Legends IV, 22 April 2010: Omega retained the Scorpion Fighting Title by pinning Iceman in the Scorpion Cage XXX match after a choke slam. Courage 112, 20 May 2010: Omega retained the Scorpion Fighting Title when Khristain Keller could not beat a standing 15-count. Courage 114, 3 June 2010: Omega retained the Scorpion Fighting Title when Fejona Min could not beat a standing 60-count. Courage 115, 10 June 2010: Omega retained the Scorpion Fighting Title when Rory Hayes could not beat a standing 15-count. Fight Night 2010, 24 June 2010: Omega won the Scorpion Fight Night Challenge II with 14 points to Fejona Min's 12 and kept the Scorpion Fighting Title.

Five HDTV title matches sit inside the bracket and Johnny Borealis is named in every one of them; the fed's own title log names no champion on any of them. The win itself stays bracketed — "for almost an entire year" and "the better part of a year" in two later cards are consistent with it and do not date it. The record spells the character both 'Jonathan Borealis' and 'Johnny Borealis'.

reigns_index.h: 15 August 2011 · GCW (gcwonline.net)'The SoCal Prophet' Brad Cruz — Hardcore Championship won at WorldWide 152 until 10 January 2012 Sources disagree — the fed's own title list still names Bryan Mayhem the champion, which four later cards contradict outright: the vacating (Mayhem retired), the award to Cruz, the announcement "Here is your winner...the GCW Hardcore Champion...BRAD CRUZ!" and the unification match in which he loses it. The list was not kept current after 2010 and is recorded as stale, not as evidence. Recorded on the night itself, and not smoothed: the commentary disputes the award before it happens — "Yale: I think there needs to be some official way for it since he never officially beat Mayhem" — and both men object to the letter afterwards. One successful defence is held, and it is the Vanguard unification: Rampage of 11 Oct 2011, billed "a one-title-leaves match", won on the Cruzifix Slam — "Andrews: Here is your winner...the GCW Hardcore Champion...The SoCal Prophet...BRAAAAAAD! CRUUUUUUUUUUUUZZZZZZZ!!!" and closing "Bryan: What a war that was, and we've got a solidified Hardcore Champion!" The commentary of 10 Jan 2012 calls that match "his first actual defense of the belt", which does not count the unification as one; both statements stand.

reigns_index.s: united states championship | gcw (gcwonline.net) | johnny borealis |  | johnny borealis
reigns_index.h: 30 September 2011 · GCW (gcwonline.net)Johnny Borealis — United States Championship won at WorldWide 154 until 11 October 2011 Sources disagree — his own bio card reads 'World Champion, 3x TV Champ, 3x US Champ', and he says the same in the federation's own voice on the card: 'Now that I've got the GCW United States Title for the third time in my life'. The record carries two United States reigns for him — this one and reign No. 15 (2005-08-28 to 2005-11-27, won as 'Jonathan Borealis'). Both readings are recorded; no third reign is filed, because no page row, title-log entry or match text stages one. A reign the federation's own United States Title History page does not carry (the page stops in 2009). The belt changed hands twice in one night through the same American Dream mix-up: Fujita left with the Television title and Borealis with the United States title, and GCW's own Board member Triumph Frost ratified both on the spot. He never defended it. The end is a forfeit, not a loss: the federation's own commentary says he 'gave it up' and 'left it in the center of the ring' to take the Rampage final, and the belt was won from vacant the same night (see the next reign).

reigns_index.h: unknown · AAWC (All Action, 1993)Hot Shot — AAWC World Heavyweight Championship end unknown (The record does not say how Hot Shot won the title.) The earliest AAWC championship fact anywhere in the held record. the CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history (promotions/cswa/archive/unified-world-heavyweight-championship-history-1997.html) records that "AAWC World Champion Hot Shot" took part in the IRONMAN of CHAMPIONS at the CSWA's LAST CALL II on 24 October 1993, in the finals of which Hornet defeated Joey Melton, "merging the IWCCW World, AAWC World, and the ten-title CSWA Unified Championship." The reign is recorded as ending with that merge because the title itself was merged; the record does not say what became of Hot Shot's own hold on it. The AAWC bills an AAWC World Heavyweight Championship again on its own card of 25 October 1996, three years later, and nothing held explains how the belt came back.

reigns_index.h: unknown · VWF (Vegas, 2001–2005)Lark Fenriz — VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship until 12 October 2004 (Champion by the promotion's own billing after the February 2004 vacancy; the winning match is not in the held record.) Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing, on the same footing as the wing's other off-air title changes; the crowning show is absent from the record. Continues to be billed champion on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), scratched from his own three-way match by majority owner Kingston Cash before the bell; returns to competition, without the title on the line, in an eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Retains the title in a clean pin over Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004). The Heavyweight Championship main event on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) ends without a finish when a returning Classy Joey Boy interferes; Kingston Cash announces a random-draw title tournament running each week until Vegas Violence, with the champion defending every time he is drawn and the title changing hands on count-outs and disqualifications during it. Retains cleanly over a returning Billy Bones, a shell of his former self after months in an alcoholic rehabilitation facility, in the tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004). Wrestles The Predator Kevin Simmons to a time-limit draw in the tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004); majority owner Kingston Cash rules the count-out and disqualification stipulation does not cover draws, and both men advance. Retains in a fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) over Classy Joey Boy, Sebastian and The Assassin Marcus O'Malley (self-eliminated to save a kidnapped Mark McQueen), pinning Sebastian with the Sammael after Sebastian tricks Classy Joey Boy into a sledgehammer disqualification; the win sets a Vegas Violence main event against tournament runner-up The Equalizer. Signs the contract for that match on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), where a video appearance by Jason Storm inserts him into the match as a third man and the champion declares he no longer cares about the title, only about denying The Equalizer. Loses the title to The Equalizer in a three-way also involving Jason Storm at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), pinned after a chair shot from guest referee Flash; Orion's own interference in the match, and a referee dispute between guest referees Classy Joey Boy and Flash, both factor into the finish.
